title: Accepted idea delivery to the main branch

description.need: An accepted idea that nobody carries to the main branch is a decision that never happened, and the work already exists in pieces that each own a different hand-off: one triages, one implements, one gives a test verdict, one releases. Nothing owns the item's identity from accepted to merged, nothing re-checks the idea against the code as it stands before building it, and nothing looks afterwards to see whether the change did what the idea claimed.
description.input: One accepted item with whatever evidence was attached when it was accepted, the code it names as it stands today, the repository's own conventions and checks, and whatever authority the operator has granted this work.
description.coreAction: Carry one accepted item all the way to a reviewable, verified change on the main branch: re-validate it against the current code with the authority to decline and say why, derive the checklist that will prove it done, implement it in an isolated branch, let the repository's own checks and tests be the standard, deliver a pull request or a ready branch where no hosted review surface exists, and after the merge check the claim the idea made.
description.output: A merged or review-ready change scoped to exactly one accepted item, with the checks that were run and what they returned, a checklist a reviewer can walk, an outcome written back on the item, and either a measurement confirming the item's claim or a plain note that it did not hold.

activities.label: Read the accepted item and its evidence against the code as it stands today
Decide go, decline or split, and write the checklist that will prove it done
Implement the change on its own branch, scoped to the item and nothing else
Run the repository's own gates and tests, and fix what they find
Deliver the change for review with the checklist and the evidence attached
After the merge, check whether the claim the item made actually held
Write the outcome back on the item and the general lesson back on the recipe

outcomes.statement: Every accepted item taken up reaches one of three ends, and none of them is silence.
successCriteria: The item's record carries the branch or the review request, the decline with its evidence, or the blocker and who can decide it
No item is left with work on disk and nothing written down
The change touches only what the item was accepted for, and anything else noticed becomes a new item

outcomes.statement: The idea is checked against the code as it stands before a line of it is written.
successCriteria: The run names the code it read and what it found there
An item the current code contradicts is declined with that evidence rather than built anyway
The checklist that will prove the item done is written before the change, not assembled afterwards to fit it

outcomes.statement: Nothing reaches the main branch on a check that was never run or was made to stop complaining.
successCriteria: The delivered change names which gates and tests were run and what each returned
A red result is fixed, never resolved by deleting or skipping a test, adding a suppression directive, editing the gate configuration, or moving a dependency version to quiet it
A gate broken for reasons unrelated to this item is escalated rather than worked around

outcomes.statement: The claim the idea made is checked after the change is on the main branch.
successCriteria: The post-merge read names what was observed and whether the claimed effect happened
A claim that did not hold is written on the item rather than quietly dropped
A lesson that would help the next item of this shape is proposed against the recipe, not kept in one run's notes

guidance: Carry the item you were given; everything else you notice becomes another item. Never make a check pass by deleting a test, silencing a warning, editing the gate it is judged by, or bumping a dependency to quiet it: each turns a red signal green without making anything true. Shipping to the default branch is the operator's authority unless the mandate grants it, so a branch and a review request is where you stop. Blocked is a result: name what you need, leave the branch reviewable, and end.

connectorRoles.note: the local checkout the change is written and proved in
the hosted surface the change is offered on; optional, and unbound where the project has none

recommendedTrigger.rationale: An idea reaching accepted is a real event, decided by a person, and the moment work is expected to start from it. A self-paced fallback still earns its place beside it, because accepted items go quiet: an item nobody woke on is exactly the failure this work exists to end, and a periodic sweep for accepted items with no branch and no decline catches it.

personalizationNeeds: Which repository and which of its branches is the default, because the whole scope discipline rests on knowing which branch is not yours to write to
How far this work may go on its own, from opening a branch through to merging one, since that boundary belongs to the operator and cannot be inferred from the repository
Where accepted items live and how an outcome is written back onto one, because an outcome recorded nowhere is the same as no outcome
Which checks are the real gate here, since every repository has checks that block and checks that only advise, and treating the second kind as the first stalls work that was fine
Whether a hosted review surface exists at all, because the deliverable is a pull request where one does and a ready branch with a written checklist where none does
dependencies: git, since the work creates a branch and commits in a real checkout
the repository's own gates and test suite, installed and runnable locally, because the third outcome depends on running them rather than trusting them
a command line client for the hosted review surface, wherever one exists, since the delivery step posts the change rather than describing it

examples.title: A registered local checkout in the repository role, driven by the Claude Code CLI
examples.notes: builtin-codebase carries create_branch, apply_diff, run_tests, get_git_status and commit_changes, which covers the whole local half: branch, change, prove, commit. The CLI is the thing doing the work in that checkout rather than a connector, so its own conventions file is read as part of re-validation, and the branch it is given is the one it stays on.

examples.title: A hosted repository in the review_surface role, with gh opening the pull request
examples.notes: gh pr create is enough for the delivery step, and the checklist and the gate results go in the pull request body where a reviewer reads them without asking. builtin-github's documented PAT scopes (Contents read, Issues and Pull requests read and write) cover posting and answering but not reading Actions or check runs, so the verdict this work reports is always the suite it ran itself in the branch.

examples.title: A plain git repository with no hosted review surface
examples.notes: The review_surface role goes unbound and the deliverable changes shape rather than disappearing: a named branch pushed or left in place, plus the checklist and the gate results written where the operator will read them. Nothing about the scope rung changes, and the post-merge check runs against the default branch once the operator has merged it.

inputSchema.name: item_id
inputSchema.description: The accepted item to carry, by its id. One item per run: a run that widens its own scope is the failure this work exists to prevent.

inputSchema.name: project_id
inputSchema.description: Optional project the item belongs to, for a backlog spanning more than one repository where the item's own record does not name it.
